notes: 2000 independent single-task workflow runs (no DAG, no parents), bulk-triggered with the TypeScript SDK's runManyNoWait -> BulkTriggerWorkflow gRPC, which the SDK splits into 4 chunks of 500 (its default batchSize) sent serially. Pre-enqueue is real: the worker is paused through PATCH /api/v1/workers/{id} {isPaused:true} before the bulk trigger and unpaused immediately after it returns, so all 2000 rows are QUEUED before any slot is filled. Hatchet's default slot count is 100; it was set to 20 (worker option slots: 20) so every engine in this study runs at the same concurrency. One discarded warmup + 5 measured reps, 60s idle between reps, 90s settle after the worker connected. Timings are Hatchet's own: created_at from v1_tasks_olap.inserted_at, started_at/completed_at from the STARTED and FINISHED rows in v1_task_events_olap. Only the sleeping workload was measured: a naive fibo in Node is about ten times faster than in CPython, so a CPU-bound body would compare V8 against CPython rather than the engine against itself. In every rep exactly 20 of the 2000 tasks (one slot set) carry a started_at earlier than the last chunk's inserted_at: the pause takes effect a beat after the first dispatch. 20 tasks out of 2000 at the head of a 16.7s window does not move the throughput figure, and the earlier Python run shows the same offset (first_start_after_last_enqueue_s was negative there too), so the two runs are comparable on this point.
outlier_note: Rep 3 is an outlier at 88.176/s. Its per-second start histogram shows the cause: the first 20 tasks (one full slot set) start, run and finish, then nothing is dispatched for 5-6 seconds, after which the queue drains at the normal ~125 starts/s. Removing those 5-6 idle seconds puts the rep back in line with the other four. The same stall appears in the discarded warmup here, and in two of the five reps of the earlier Python 20x1 sleep control on this same harness, so it is a property of the engine under the pause/unpause pre-enqueue trick, not of either SDK. The median of five reps is unaffected by it.
mean_occupancy_note: mean_concurrency is the time-weighted occupancy of the 20 slots over the measured span: 11.9 of 20 in the four clean reps, 8.8 in the stalled rep. The engine never oversubscribed (peak 20, zero time above 20) and spent only ~1-2% of the span with all 20 slots busy.

python_run.source: the earlier run of this study, same engine image digest, same instance type, same stock config, same 1 worker x 20 slots, same 2000-task sleeping workload

comparison_python_sdk.verdict: The language does not change Hatchet's throughput. 119.2/s with the TypeScript SDK against 115.6/s with the Python SDK is a 3.1% difference on a workload whose body costs the same 100ms in both, with the engine leaving 40% of the 20 slots idle in both cases (mean occupancy 11.9 vs 11.5 out of 20). The ceiling is the engine's dispatch loop, not the SDK's language.
